# Teacher Forcing

**Formal definition.** Teacher forcing conditions each training prediction on the observed target prefix rather than on tokens previously generated by the model. For source $x$ and target $y_{1:T}$, the conditional sequence likelihood factorizes as $p_\theta(y_{1:T}\mid x)=\prod_{t=1}^T p_\theta(y_t\mid y_{<t},x)$. The decoder receives the target shifted right, typically beginning with a start token, and its output at position $t$ is scored against $y_t$. The autoregressive factorization is exact; the model's conditional probabilities are learned approximations. A causal attention mask prevents a training position from accessing later shifted inputs, so all target positions can be evaluated in parallel without revealing the answer.

**Why it matters here.** At inference the true target prefix is unavailable, so generated tokens are fed back sequentially. Errors can therefore change later contexts, producing a training–inference distribution mismatch often called exposure bias. Teacher forcing does not itself guarantee accurate free-running generation, and parallel training does not make autoregressive inference parallel across output positions.
